newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch call for EU crime prevention network.
newsitem.headline: Dutch call for EU crime prevention network.

text.p: The EU should set up an official crime prevention network so members can learn from each others' experience and cooperate in crime prevention, Dutch Justice Minister Winnie Sorgdrager said on Monday.

Sorgdrager told an EU seminar that fighting crime solely by increasing police and cell numbers and handing out stiffer sentences ultImately constituted a threat to the quality of life in free and democratic societies in the EU.

"If we Europeans wish to prevent an explosive growth in our prison systems - like that in the United States - we need effective policies to prevent rather than just combat crime," Sorgdrager told the seminar.
The Netherlands holds the EU's six-month presidency until the end of June.
She argued that crime prevention should tackle offences outside of "traditional" areas such as burglary or street crime -- aiming to prevent environmental crimes or corruption.
Sorgdrager said crime prevention measures had been vindicated in the Netherlands, contributing to stabilising crime figures over the the past 10 years, and even a reduction in crime since 1996.
EU countries currently fight crime through the Europol police agency, which coordinates the exchange of information between the 15-country bloc's national police forces.
